chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Drummers who came to Minton's to learn
summary: Blakey, Max Roach, Big Sid, Don Lamond and Tiny Kahn came to learn the new approach; Gene Krupa did not.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Oh, my God. Every drummer you can think of.

Art Blakey. Max Roach. Big Sid Catlett. Don Lamond. Tiny Kahn. Every drummer in New York. Because it was after Big Sid had told everyone how wonderful it was, how much had to be done, and how it could be developed into something fantastic, then everyone came to learn the base.
What it was built upon. What it was all about.
Did any of those other drummers -- did Gene Krupa come up?
No, Gene Krupa didn't come up.
Gene used to come listen to Chick all the time.
Yeah, well that was more his style.
Yeah. He couldn't make that switch, could he?
